description.narrative: The Regional Leadership Programme (RLP) is designed to meet Africa’s leadership needs and supportthe accelerated achievement of Agenda 2030 and Agenda 2063, in alignment with the UNDP StrategicPlan, the Regional Bureau for Africa’s (RBA) Revised Strategic Offer for Africa, the Regional ProgrammeDocument, and the Renewed Governance and Peacebuilding Framework for Africa.The RLP builds upon a key foundational enabler of the RBA Strategic Offer - the Governance of Things -which aims to “invest in the development of targeted leadership capacities at both national and sub-national levels.” Additionally, the RLP addresses Outcome 1 of the Regional Programme Document: African citizens (especially women and youth), in a context of reinvigorated social contracts, have astronger voice and influence in policymaking and implementation processes within the African Union andregional economic communities. Pillar 3 of the Renewed Governance and Peacebuilding Framework forAfrica seeks to “provide platforms to bring together stakeholders at the national and local levels towards acommon viewpoint on economic governance”, while Pillar 6 focuses on the “Capacity of states’ corefunctions enhanced to promote local economic development” and targets “Local governance capacity ofMember States enhanced to localize and implement Agenda 2030 and Agenda 2063”

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

The Implementing Partner shall ensure that all of its obligations set forth under the section entitled “Legal Context and/or Risk Management Standard Clauses” are passed on to each responsible party, subcontractor and sub-recipient and that all the clauses under this section entitled “Risk Management” are included, mutatis mutandis, in all sub-contracts or sub-agreements entered into further to the Project Document
